title: Playing alone with guitar, kazoo and harmonica
summary: Pete repeats his cigar-box guitar story and says he played by himself with guitar and kazoo.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Uh, no, I can stop. Just for a second, I want to get an idea. Okay. Hey, that was a guitar you took up.
Yes. I made my first guitar. Mm-hmm.
I made it out of cigar box.
I used this brass. Copper wire.
Five strings. And I learned on that. Mm-hmm. And I got really interest in it.

I went and bought me old cheap guitar. Oh, the strings was sitting just about an inch from the neck. But I went on with it. Right. Finally, I run across a really good guitar. And that's why I learned really good. And I just picked it up and went on. Music for getting to follow me then.
Did you play with bands or alone or both or what?
No, I only played it by myself alone.
Just played guitar and blow one of those kazoofs there.
Yeah. Never had a watch board or anything with you?

No, so never have. Well, I played harmonica a little but not too much. As I got to smoking and wind got a little short, well, I laid the harmonica aside. Mm-hmm. And that's kept up with the guitar. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. So I've been trying to stop playing music, but it's just a little like to me, I can't put it down. And the time I get a hold of one guitar and I'll maybe sell it or give it to somebody. Well, music just come back to me and worry me, so I just have to go back and buy me another guitar.
